label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 1 · Question 8

hints.title: Name the unknown side
hints.body: Put XZ=t. Sketch the two possible triangles on the same fixed side and ray. Apply the cosine rule using the given angle at X and the two sides meeting there.
hints.recap: The cosine rule links the third side to two sides and their included angle.
hints.pitfall: Keep both possible positive roots for t.
hints.pause: Substitute the known lengths and solve the quadratic for t.

recall.reminder: The cosine rule links the third side to two sides and their included angle.

hints.title: Compare the areas
hints.body: Use 12XY·XZsin30∘ for each triangle. Cancel the factors that are the same in both areas.
hints.recap: Shared factors cancel when taking a ratio.
hints.pitfall: S is the larger triangle, so put its area first.
hints.pause: Use the two side lengths to find the requested area ratio.

recall.reminder: Shared factors cancel when taking a ratio.

solution:
1. Write a quadratic for the unknown side. Set XZ=t. The cosine rule gives a2=3a2+t2−23atcos30∘=3a2+t2−3at.

2. Keep both triangles. t2−3at+2a2=(t−a)(t−2a)=0, giving t=a or t=2a. Since a is a side length, a>0; both triangles are nondegenerate.

3. Compare areas. Each area is 12(3a)tsin30∘, so area is proportional to t. The larger-to-smaller ratio is 2a:a=2:1. Answer B.
knowledgePattern: Retain both cosine-rule triangles and compare their common-height areas
